## 3. Mandatory-requirements outlook (NO scored functionality in this pack)

This pack has **no functionality matrix and no numeric threshold**: Stage 1
is administrative compliance + mandatory requirements (§5.1, pass/fail),
Stage 2 is straight 80/20 price + specific goals. The SDK's
`functionality_threshold`/`passes_functionality` pair is **not applicable**
— the first sample of the set where the correct value is "none", a useful
negative case against the corpus distribution (n=238, mode 70). The
practical consequence cuts the other way: with no scored middle stage,
**every §5.1 item is a binary kill** — "Near compliance is non-compliance"
applies to the proposal documents themselves, and the twelve
mandatory-requirement rows in §2 above carry the whole technical risk.

Umzansi self-assessment against the minimum specification (§4 (a)–(eee)):
the resold platform (fictional) covers omni-channel ACD ticketing,
WhatsApp integration with 4–5 digit references, email sniffer + SSL, IVR,
call recording with 18-month storage, SA hosting, 15 concurrent users,
mobile app, SMS notifications, toll-free porting of 087 147 0895 — the
spec is a feature checklist for a mainstream SA cloud contact-centre
product; the risk sits in the **service commitments** (07h00–21h00
Mon–Sun support desk; on-site technician 07:00–16:00 weekdays for the
full term; 2-hour major-fault response with **monetary compensation
credits** for breaches) which must be priced, not just promised.

## 4. Price & preference (80/20) — the pack's own 3-year schedule

**Term note (recorded neutrally):** per client domain knowledge, Musina
contract terms were believed to run 5 years. **This pack states 3 years /
36 months throughout** — the title, ToR §1 ("three (3) years/thirty six
(36) months"), and pricing instruction §6(a) ("covering the cost of
providing the specified service over a period of three (3) years") — so
the quotation is built to the pack's own 3-year term, unlike sample 4
where the advert's term and the category norm diverged. First Musina pack
on file; one pack is one data point, not a norm.

The pack's pricing schedule (pages 11–12) is itself a **year-by-year
grid** — Once-Off / Monthly / Annual columns for Year 1, Year 2, Year 3
plus per-unit call tariffs and a 3-year VAT-inclusive total ("The call
tariffs are costed on a unit cost basis, and the actual variable value
thereof will be dependent on call activity") — direct pack-text evidence
for the multi-year pricing-model gap (F-06). No escalation formula is
prescribed; GCC §17 defaults an unqualified price to "a fixed delivery
price", so the mock schedule is flat-rated across the term.

| Component | Basis | Amount (incl VAT) |
|-----------|-------|-------------------|
| Once-off: implementation + migration R185,000 · mobile app R120,000 · hardware (15 phones + headsets, reverts to municipality at term end) R96,750 · training R78,000 · IVR/call-back/voice supervision R24,000 | one-off | R503,750.00 |
| Recurring: licensing 15 users R28,500 + VoIP/SIP R6,900 + WhatsApp R4,200 + SMS R2,750 + email sniffer/SSL R1,450 + recording/backup R3,900 + support & maintenance R9,800 = **R57,500/month** | 36 months | R2,070,000.00 |
| **Quotation total (QTN-2026-00341)** | | **R2,573,750.00** |

- Worked example from SDK `price_points`: Umzansi at R2,573,750 vs a
  hypothetical lowest compliant offer of R2,300,000 scores **70.48 / 80**.
  Cloud contact-centre licensing is a crowded resale market — the
  recurring stream (80% of the offer) is where undercutting happens.
- Specific goals (20): HDI 51%+ black-owned → fictional 67% claims the
  **10**; women's equity 51% → not met (1 of 3 directors) → 0/4;
  disability → 0/3; youth → 0/3. **Umzansi claims 10/20**, evidenced via
  the comprehensive CSD report route the pack itself prescribes
  (SCORE-PREF-CLAIM: no proof, no points). A 51% women-owned competitor
  starts 4 points up — on 80/20 arithmetic that is ≈R115k of price room.
- The pack's **legacy preference layer** (Form C HDI equity, Form D 1939
  local content/SABS) must still be completed — Form C "Failure … to fill
  in and/or to sign the certificate will be interpreted to mean that point
  preference is not claimed", and Form D non-completion forfeits any
  local-content consideration. Operative scoring stays the MBD 6.1 table.

## 5. Risk notes

1. **The service-level tail is the real cost.** A staffed 07h00–21h00
   seven-day support commitment plus a weekday on-site technician for 36
   months, with compensation credits on 2h/48h response breaches, dwarfs
   the software margin for a small ICT unit. Sizing that desk honestly
   decides whether R57,500/month is a price or a promise.
2. **Rates clearance for company AND every director** — the classic
   municipal killer, demanded twice in this pack; three directors, <3
   months freshness, plus the MBD 8 arrears question. Start day one.
3. **Every technical returnable is pass/fail.** With no scored
   functionality stage there is no partial credit: a missing appointment
   letter on one of the three references (§5.1(f)) is a Stage-1 death,
   not a dropped point.
4. **Distance:** Port Shepstone (KZN) to Musina (Limpopo) is ≈1,300km;
   the on-site technician commitment effectively requires a local
   presence or subcontract — and Form C caps subcontracting at 25% where
   preference is claimed.
5. **Hardware reverts to the municipality** at contract end (spec (eee))
   and carries a 36-month warranty — price it as a sunk supply, not an
   asset.

## 6. Recommendation

**Merits verdict (as inside the window): GO.** The specification is a
mainstream cloud contact-centre feature list; both quantitative signals
are computable and positive (80/20 confirmed by value; no functionality
threshold to fail); all fatal gates open at readout (rates statements,
bank rating letter) were curable well inside a normal runway; auto-fill on
the generated MBD set is 97.1%. The deciding factors are commercial, not
compliance: the 7-day support desk and on-site technician economics, and
the 4-point specific-goals handicap.

**Calendar verdict (build date 2026-08-20): NO-BID — window closed.**
Closing passed on 11 May 2026; late is dead, no exceptions (KILL-01). The
value of this sample is demonstrative: full-pack grounding with a fired
deadline kill, a pack with no functionality stage, and the
mandatory-requirements-as-gates evaluation pattern. Watch for a re-advert
— municipal system tenders of this shape recur at contract expiry.
